Prime Minister’s Rural Development Fellows Scheme — Prime Minister’s Rural Development Fellows Scheme
Scheme: Prime Minister’s Rural Development Fellows Scheme SECTION: Ministry: Ministry Of Rural Development Department: Department of Rural Development SECTION: Level: Central Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme Target beneficiaries: Individual SECTION: Overview The scheme aims to provide short term catalytic support to the District Administration in backward districts to improve programme delivery and simultaneously develop a cadre of Development Facilitators. Fellows receive professional experience, structured learning, and a monthly stipend. Detailed description The scheme "Prime Minister’s Rural Development Fellows Scheme" by the Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, aims to provide a short-term work opportunity for young women and men who possess academic or professional expertise that will serve the district administration in improving programme delivery and interface with the marginalized section of the population, thereby aiming to reduce developmental and governance deficits. The scheme provides structured learning and hands-on professional experience in rural development and poverty reduction, offering Fellows opportunities to act as Development Facilitators and assist District Administration, particularly in backward districts, while participating in a post-graduate degree programme through distance learning and contact sessions, leading to a post-graduate degree in Development Practice. SECTION: Benefits SECTION: Stipend Package The Fellow shall be entitled to a consolidated stipend package of ₹50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) per month during the orientation period. The Fellow shall be entitled to ₹75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand only) per month during the first year of the Fellowship (post-orientation). The Fellow shall receive a 10% increment during the second year, subject to satisfactory performance. This package is deemed to cover the Fellow’s honorarium, boarding and lodging expenses during orientation, accommodation/house rent during the rest of the Fellowship period, health insurance, life and disability insurance cover, and any other contingency expenses. Travel reimbursement will be based on actual costs and restricted to AC-II tier train fare by the shortest route or equivalent, plus local transport cost. Women Fellows with children below five years are allowed the travel cost of a care-giver if the care-giver accompanies the Fellow with her child. SECTION: Other Benefits Participation in a post graduate degree programme through distance learning and contact sessions leading to a post graduate degree in Development Practice. Award of a Fellowship Certificate and an appropriate post graduate degree in Development Practice upon satisfactory completion of engagement and course requirements. Office facilities made available by the District Collector, including suitable space, a computer/laptop, and internet connectivity free of charge. Provision of suitable modes of transport by District administration while travelling within the district for regular work. Disbursement of Stipend During the orientation programme, the stipend shall be paid by the National Rural Livelihood Promotion Society through the Programme Mentor. Post-placement, the National Rural Livelihood Promotion Society shall pay the monthly stipend to

The second-year increment is subject to the Fellow’s satisfactory performance as determined by the National Rural Livelihood Promotion Society in consultation with the Programme Mentor. SECTION: Conditions *It is mandatory for the Fellows to purchase suitable health insurance and life and disability insurance coverage for the entire duration of the Fellowship, including the orientation period. *The Fellow shall not take up any type of employment with any other person, firm, or agency during the tenure of the Fellowship. *On successful completion of Fellowship, the Fellow is required to spend at least one year in public service as a paid full-time employee of the State Rural Livelihood Mission in the State she/he is assigned to. *Failure to join or complete the required one year of public service mandates the Fellow to return to the National Rural Livelihood Promotion Society the entire amount spent on academic programmes during the Fellowship (including orientation), plus an amount equivalent to the stipend of the last three months of the Fellowship period as compensation. SECTION: Exclusions The applicant, who has been provisionally selected in the final result sheet for Prime Minister’s Rural Development Fellowship in an earlier stint, will not be allowed to avail the fellowship if he/she did not complete the full term of that prior Fellowship. SECTION: Eligibility The applicant should be a citizen of India. The applicant's age must be between 22 years and 27 years at the time of application. The applicant must hold at least a graduate degree from a recognized University with a four-year degree course. The applicant must hold a post-graduate degree from a recognized University in case the graduate degree course duration was less than four years. The applicant's one-year post graduate course will also be considered valid for eligibility if it is regular, full time, and if the degree/equivalent diploma is recognized by the All India Council for Technical Education/Medical Council of India/University Grants Commission. The applicant must have achieved at least 50% marks in the aggregate or equivalent grade at the graduate or Post-graduate level, whichever is qualifying.

text:
Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan — Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan
SECTION: Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan SECTION: Ministry: Ministry Of Health & Family Welfare Department: Department of Health and Family Welfare SECTION: Level: Central Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme Target beneficiaries: Individual SECTION: Overview The scheme aims to provide fixed-day assured, comprehensive and quality antenatal care universally to all pregnant women in 2nd and 3rd trimester on the 9th of every month. It offers free comprehensive antenatal care services at government health facilities. Detailed description The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan" was launched on 9th June 2016 by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, aims to provide fixed-day assured, comprehensive and quality antenatal care universally to all pregnant women (in 2nd and 3rd trimester) on the 9th of every month, addressing the critical need for standardized maternal healthcare services and reducing maternal and infant mortality rates across the country. The scheme provides assured, comprehensive and quality antenatal care, free of cost, universally to all pregnant women on the 9th of every month and includes a minimum package of antenatal care services provided by Obstetrics and Gynaecology specialists, Radiologists, and Physicians at government health facilities. The applicant must be a pregnant woman in her 2nd or 3rd trimester of pregnancy and must be willing to visit designated government health facilities on the 9th of every month for antenatal care services. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India through National Health Mission at state and district levels and applications for this scheme are accepted both online through the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan portal and offline at designated government health facilities. SECTION: Benefits SECTION: Medical Services Provided SECTION: Comprehensive Antenatal Care: Special Antenatal Care services provided by Obstetrics and Gynaecology specialists, Radiologists, and Physicians at government health facilities. Minimum Package of Services: A minimum package of investigations and medicines such as Iron Folic Acid and calcium supplements provided to all pregnant women attending Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan clinics. SECTION: High Risk Pregnancy Identification: Identification and follow-up of high risk pregnancies with red stickers added to Mother and Child Protection cards. SECTION: Fixed Day Service: Services provided on the 9th of every month at designated facilities. SECTION: Service Delivery Mechanism SECTION: Single Window System: Using principles of single window system for providing investigations and medicines. SECTION: Mobile Application Support: Mobile and web-based application to help pregnant women find their nearest Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan facility. SECTION: Cost: Completely free of cost to all beneficiaries. SECTION: Coverage Areas SECTION: Facility Types: Services provided at Government health facilities including Primary Health Centres, Community Health Centres, District Hospitals, and urban health facilities in both urban and rural areas. SECTION: Conditions Regular attendance on the 9th of every month for antenatal check-ups. Compliance with medical advice and treatment prescribed by healthcare providers. Follow-up visits as recommended for high-risk pregnancies. Carrying

The applicant must be in 2nd trimester (13-28 weeks) or 3rd trimester (29-40 weeks) of pregnancy. SECTION: Special Categories The applicant identified as high-risk pregnancy cases receive priority attention and follow-up care. The applicant who are dropouts from regular antenatal care services are encouraged to participate. Question: At what stage of my pregnancy can I start accessing the comprehensive antenatal care services provided under this national maternal health initiative? Answer: You can access services if you are in your 2nd or 3rd trimester of pregnancy, meaning you must have completed the first trimester (beyond 12 weeks of gestation). Question: What type of medical specialists will provide antenatal care services to me when I visit the designated health facility on the scheduled day? Answer: You will receive care from Obstetrics and Gynaecology specialists, Radiologists, and Physicians as part of the comprehensive antenatal care package at government health facilities. Question: How can I locate the nearest health facility participating in this monthly antenatal care program using digital resources available to pregnant women? Question: When was this national maternal health program launched and which government ministry is responsible for its implementation across the country? Question: What types of government health facilities participate in providing these monthly antenatal care services under this comprehensive maternal health initiative? Question: What specific medical investigations and screening procedures will be conducted during my monthly antenatal care visits under this standardized healthcare program? SECTION: Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana Ministry: Ministry Of Labour and Employment SECTION: Level: Central Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme Target beneficiaries: Individual SECTION: Overview The scheme aims to stimulate employment creation, increase workforce formalization, and enhance employability. It provides financial incentives to first-time employees and offers wage subsidies to eligible employers for creating sustained jobs, especially in manufacturing. Detailed description The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana" was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India. The scheme aims to promote the generation of sustained additional employment, increase the formalization of the workforce, and enhance employability. The scheme provides comprehensive financial assistance to first-time employees to navigate their learning curve and incentivizes eligible establishments, particularly in the manufacturing sector, for generating sustained additional employment over their established baseline. The applicant must regularly file the Electronic Challan-cum-Return along with provident fund contributions and fulfill the defined threshold criteria for new employment generation. The scheme is implemented by the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. The applications for this scheme are accepted continuously during the registration period from 01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027 through the online updating of establishment details and employee Aadhaar authentication on the official portal. SECTION: Benefits SECTION: Part A: SECTION: First-Timer Benefits The scheme provides a one-time incentive of up to ₹15,000/- to assist first-time employees. The first installment is up to a maximum of ₹7,500/-, calculated as half of the average Employees' Provident Fund wage for six continuous completed months. The second installment is equal to the average of the twelve completed months' Employees' Provident Fund wage reduced by the first installment, restricted to a total incentive of ₹15,000/-. The second installment will be kept in an appropriate saving instrument or deposit account for a specified period. The incentives to the employees shall be paid through Direct Benefit Transfer using the Aadhaar Bridge Payment System to their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts. The incentive shall be disbursed within 45 days after fulfilling the eligibility condition and filing of the paid Electronic Challan-cum-Return. SECTION: Part B: Support to Employers The scheme provides incentives to the employer for two years in respect of employment generated over and above the baseline. For the manufacturing sector, the incentive to the employer will continue for the third and the fourth year. For additional employees with an Employees' Provident Fund wage less than or equal to ₹10,000/-, the benefit to the employer is up to ₹1,000/- per additional employment per month. In respect of employees getting Employees' Provident Fund wages below ₹10,000/-, the incentive at the rate of 10 percent of the Employees' Provident Fund wage will be provided as an additional risk mitigation measure. For additional employees with an Employees' Provident Fund wage greater than ₹10,000/- and up to ₹20,000/-, the

The applicant must not have pending or decided inquiries relating to irregularities under the Atmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana scheme. The applicant must join an establishment during the scheme registration period from 01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027. The applicant must have their Universal Account Number authenticated by Face Authentication Technology on the UMANG Application. The applicant must have gross wages up to ₹1,00,000/- per month at the time of joining the establishment. The applicant must have Electronic Challan-cum-Returns along with contributions filed for six continuous months. National Savings (Monthly Income Account) Scheme — Scheme: National Savings (Monthly Income Account) Scheme
SECTION: Scheme: National Savings (Monthly Income Account) Scheme SECTION: Ministry: Ministry Of Finance Department: Department of Financial Service SECTION: Level: Central Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme Target beneficiaries: Individual SECTION: Overview The scheme provides a fixed monthly income to investors through periodic interest payments on a one-time deposit made at the time of account opening. Detailed description The National Savings (Monthly Income Account) Scheme, 2019, popularly known as the Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS), is a government-backed small savings scheme administered by the Ministry of Finance. The scheme provides a fixed monthly income to investors through periodic interest payments on a one-time deposit made at the time of account opening. The scheme is designed for individuals seeking a secure investment option with regular monthly returns. Accounts can be opened individually, jointly by up to three adults, or on behalf of eligible minors. SECTION: Key Features Government-backed savings scheme with assured returns. Single deposit account with no recurring contributions. Monthly interest payout to the account holder. Account tenure of 5 years. Joint accounts permitted with up to three adults. Nomination facility available as per applicable rules. Transfer of an account from one post office to another is permitted. Multiple accounts may be opened subject to the prescribed deposit limits. SECTION: Benefits SECTION: Deposit Limits Minimum Deposit: ₹1,000 and thereafter in multiples of ₹1,000. Maximum Deposit in Single Account: ₹4,50,000. Maximum Deposit in Minor Account/Account opened by Guardian: ₹4,50,000. Maximum Deposit in Joint Account: ₹9,00,000. SECTION: Interest Interest Rate: 7.6% per annum (as specified in the 2019 notification; subject to revision by the Government from time to time). Interest is payable monthly from the date of deposit. Unclaimed monthly interest does not earn additional interest. SECTION: Maturity The account matures after 5 years from the date of opening. On maturity, the deposited amount along with eligible interest is payable to the account holder upon submission of the prescribed application. SECTION: Premature Closure Premature closure is allowed after completion of one year from the date of account opening: Closure before completion of 3 years: Deduction of 2% of the principal deposit. Closure after 3 years but before maturity: Deduction of 1% of the principal deposit. Death of Account Holder In the event of the account holder's death before maturity, the account may be closed and the deposit refunded along with interest up to the month preceding the month of refund, as per applicable rules. SECTION: Eligibility The applicant must be a citizen of India. The applicant must be residing in India. The account may be opened by a single adult. National Savings (Monthly Income Account) Scheme — Eligibility
Eligibility The applicant must be a citizen of India. The applicant must be residing in India. The account may be opened by a single adult. The account may be opened jointly by up to three adults. A minor who has attained the age of 10 years may open and operate the account in his/her own name. A guardian may open the account on behalf of a minor or a person of unsound mind. Application process SECTION: Offline To open an account under Post Office Monthly Income Scheme, follow the steps given below The applicant visits the nearest post office. Obtain Form-1 for opening a monthly income account. Fill in the application form with the required details. Attach the prescribed supporting documents. Submit the completed application form at the post office. Deposit a minimum amount of ₹1,000 or any amount in multiples of ₹1,000, subject to the prescribed maximum limit. The Post Office will verify the application and supporting documents. Upon successful verification, the Monthly Income Account will be opened under the scheme. Required documents Passport-size photograph Proof of Identity (Passport / Voter ID card / Driving License / Aadhaar Card) Proof of Address Birth Certificate (for minor applicants, if applicable) Frequently asked questions Question: What is the maturity period of the Monthly Income Account Scheme? Answer: The account matures after 5 years from the date of opening. Question: What is the minimum deposit amount? Answer: The minimum deposit amount is ₹1,000 and thereafter in multiples of ₹1,000. Question: What is the maximum deposit limit for a single account? Answer: A maximum of ₹4,50,000 can be deposited in a single account. Question: Can a joint account be opened? Answer: Yes. Up to three adults can jointly open an account. Question: Can multiple accounts be opened? Answer: Yes. An individual may open more than one account, subject to the overall deposit limits prescribed under the scheme. Question: What happens in case of the account holder's death? Answer: The account may be closed and the deposit refunded with eligible interest to the claimant as per applicable rules. Question: Is premature closure allowed? Answer: Yes. Premature closure is permitted after one year, subject to prescribed deductions. Question: Can a minor open an account? Answer: Yes. A minor aged 10 years or above may open and operate the account. Question: Is the account transferable? Answer: Yes. The account can be transferred from one post office to another in accordance with applicable rules. Question: What happens if monthly interest is not withdrawn? Answer: Unclaimed interest does not earn any additional interest.

This scheme is for pursuing higher education starting from class XI to Post Graduation courses in India. Detailed description "Post Matric Scholarship Scheme For The Students Belonging To Scheduled Tribe For Studies In India" is a centrally sponsored scheme by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, for the students of Scheduled Tribe (ST) for studies in India. This scheme is for pursuing higher education starting from class XI to Post Graduation courses in India. Objective of the scheme: To enable eligible Scheduled Tribe students to undertake quality education from Post Matric to Post Graduate level by providing them financial assistance. To create an error free platform ensuring that the targeted beneficiaries receive scholarship on time. Scholarship under the Scheme will be available to ST students for studies in India and will be directly transferred to the account of students. Scheme: Financial Assistance for Education to the Wards of Beedi/Cine/IOMC/LSDM Workers – Pre & Post-Matric Ministry: Ministry Of Labour and Employment SECTION: Level: Central Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme Target beneficiaries: Individual SECTION: Overview The scheme aims to fund the pre-matric and post-matric education of wards belonging to specific mine, beedi, and cine workers. It provides annual scholarships between ₹1,000/- and ₹25,000/- based on the student's academic level and course type. Detailed description The scheme "Financial Assistance for Education to the Wards of Beedi/Cine/IOMC/LSDM Workers – Pre & Post-Matric" was launched by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India. The scheme aims to provide educational scholarships to the children of Beedi, Iron Ore, Manganese & Chrome Ore, Limestone, Dolomite, Mica, and Cine workers. The scheme provides annual financial assistance ranging from ₹1,000/- to ₹25,000/- directly to the beneficiaries via Direct Benefit Transfer. The applicant must be studying in a recognized institution and meet the stipulated parental occupation and income thresholds. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through the National Scholarship Portal. SECTION: Benefits SECTION: Financial Assistance Rates Class I to IV (for the purchase of dress/books, etc.): ₹1,000/- per annum. Class V to VIII: ₹1,500/- per annum. Class IX: ₹2,000/- per annum. Class X: ₹2,000/- per annum. Class XI to XII: ₹3,000/- per annum. ITI: ₹6,000/- per annum. Polytechnic: ₹6,000/- per annum. Degree Courses (including B.Sc. Agriculture): ₹6,000/- per annum. Professional Courses: ₹25,000/- per annum. Mode of Disbursement: The benefits under the scheme are transferred through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system. SECTION: Exclusions The scholarship sanctioned is liable to be canceled on the following occasions If the scholar is found to have obtained a scholarship by false statements. If the scholarship discontinues his/her studies, the scholarship shall be stopped from the date of such discontinuance. If the scholar changes the subject of the course of study for which the scholarship was originally awarded or changes the Institution of Study without the prior approval of the Welfare Commissioner. If the scholar fails to make satisfactory progress in the studies or is irregular in attendance or is guilty of misconduct during the academic year for which the scholarship has been granted. If the parent(s) of the scholar ceases to be a Beedi/Mine/Cine worker. The following category of students is not eligible for the award of scholarships under the scheme Students who, after passing one stage of education, are studying in the same stage of education in a different subject. e.g. B.Sc. after B.Com. or B.Com. after B.A. or M.A. in one subject after M.A. in another subject. Students who after having completed their educational career in one professional line, continue education in a different professional line, e.g. L.L.B. after B.T.

Scheme: Short Term Fellowship under the Human Resource Development Programme for Health Research SECTION: Ministry: Ministry Of Health & Family Welfare Implementing agency: Department Of Health Research, Ministry Of Health & Family Welfare, Government Of India SECTION: Level: Central Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme Target beneficiaries: Individual SECTION: Overview The scheme aims to provide short-term advanced training and financial support to medical and health research personnel to enhance their skills and promote research in priority health areas. Detailed description The scheme "ICMR-Junior Research Fellowship" by the Department of Health Research (DHR), Ministry Of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, aims to enhance the availability of trained health research personnel through providing short-term training fellowships and financial assistance to medical faculty and researchers. It supports training in both Indian and foreign institutions for a duration of 1-3 months. The scheme focuses on priority areas such as clinical trials, genomics, toxicology, and biotechnology. It encourages multidisciplinary collaboration and the development of research projects addressing national and local health challenges. The fellowship also aims to build a skilled workforce in advanced medical and health research domains. SECTION: Benefits SECTION: For Training In Indian Institutes (1-3 Months): SECTION: Stipend: ₹40,000/- per month (if training is at a different station); ₹20,000/- per month (if training is at the same station). SECTION: Travel Support: Travelling expenses are provided as per Travelling Allowance rules of the parent organization. Contingency Grant: One-time grant up to ₹20,000/- for local travel, meetings, and related expenses. SECTION: For Training In Foreign Institutes (1-3 Months): US $3000/- per month or equivalent in other foreign currency. SECTION: Air Travel: Economy class airfare by Air India via the shortest route from parent institute to host institute. SECTION: Contingency Grant: One-time grant up to ₹30,000/- for visa, insurance, local expenses, meetings; additional ₹20,000/- for attending review meetings. SECTION: Conference Grant: US $600/- for attending conferences or institutes of interest with approval. SECTION: Eligibility Only Indian citizens working in Indian institutes are eligible. They should hold M.D./ M.S./ M.D.S. or MBBS/BDS/ MVSc./ M.Sc./M.Pharma/M.Tech or equivalent with Ph.D. in health/biomedical research. Faculty having at least three years’ experience in the college/institute as a regular employee. Persons up to 55 years of age as of the last date of receipt of application will be eligible. They should not have availed any fellowship of the duration of one month or above duration from any of the agencies of Govt. of India / State Governments for the same subject of training/research project. The fellowship is for 1-3 months. Fellowship is non-transferable. Application process SECTION: Online SECTION: Step 1: The full-length research proposals may be submitted only and no proposal in physical/hard copy is to be submitted w.r.t. the advertisements published in leading newspapers and uploaded on the websites of DHR & ICMR. Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana — Scheme: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana
SECTION: Scheme: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana SECTION: Ministry: Ministry Of Health & Family Welfare Department: Department of Health and Family Welfare SECTION: Level: Central Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme Target beneficiaries: Individual SECTION: Overview The scheme aims to provide assured, dignified, and completely free healthcare services to all pregnant women, mothers, and newborns at public health facilities. Detailed description Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana (SUMAN) is a maternity benefit initiative launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The scheme aims to provide affordable, high-quality healthcare solutions to pregnant women and newborns. Under this scheme, ensuring assured, dignified, respectful, and quality healthcare services at zero cost for all pregnant women, mothers, and newborns visiting public health facilities. Objectives of the SUMAN scheme: To achieve zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths. To ensure assured, free, and quality healthcare services for every pregnant woman and newborn. To provide dignified and respectful care, maintaining privacy and confidentiality. To enforce zero tolerance for denial of services at public health facilities. To ensure comprehensive maternal and newborn care, including antenatal, delivery, and postnatal services. SECTION: Benefits Under SUMAN, beneficiaries are entitled to the following free and cashless services at designated public health facilities: SECTION: Maternal Health Services Minimum 4 Antenatal Care (ANC) check-ups, including one in the first trimester At least one check-up under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) Free and cashless normal delivery and Caesarean section (C-section) Management of pregnancy-related complications SECTION: Newborn & Infant Care Free care for sick newborns and infants Zero-dose vaccinations (as per the government schedule) SECTION: 6 Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC) visits Early initiation and support for breastfeeding SECTION: Transport & Logistics Free transport from home to the health facility Inter-facility referral transport Drop-back facility after discharge SECTION: Other Entitlements Free drugs, diagnostics, and blood services Postnatal care and counseling, including family planning Respectful maternity care, ensuring dignity, privacy, and choice Zero out-of-pocket expenditure for all entitled services SECTION: Eligibility The applicant must be a pregnant woman. The applicant must be a mother (post-delivery) seeking services at a public health facility. Newborns aged 0 to 6 months old will be able to avail the benefits of this scheme. After delivery, lactating mothers up to 6 months from delivery are also eligible for this scheme. Application process SECTION: Offline Individuals have to visit civil hospitals in their respective areas to register themselves for the PM SUMAN Yojana. Ideally, they have to fulfill the eligibility criteria and submit the mentioned documents to register for the scheme. The civil hospitals of all the districts abide by the rules mandated by the Health Ministry. However, if there are some discrepancies, individuals can log in to the SUMAN website and file a complaint. Individuals have to submit certain documents to prove their identity. Answer: These are public health facilities that meet quality standards (NQAS/IPHS) and provide assured maternal and newborn services as per SUMAN guidelines. Answer: There are three levels: Basic Package – Primary level care BEmONC – Basic Emergency Obstetric & Newborn Care CEmONC – Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric & Newborn Care Question: What is the SUMAN Service Guarantee Charter? Answer: It is a commitment ensuring free, respectful, and quality healthcare services for every mother and newborn at SUMAN facilities. Question: How can beneficiaries register grievances under SUMAN? Answer: Grievances can be registered through: 104 toll-free helpline SUMAN web portal Help desks at facilities Question: What role do SUMAN volunteers play? Answer: Volunteers act as a bridge between the community and health system, helping beneficiaries access services, spreading awareness, and supporting emergency referrals. Question: What is the role of community institutions under SUMAN? Answer: Institutions like PRIs, SHGs, NGOs, and VHSNCs help in awareness, monitoring services, and ensuring accountability. Question: What is the incentive for reporting maternal deaths? Answer: An incentive of ₹1000 is provided to the first person who reports a maternal death through the 104 helpline (after verification).
